## Phase 3 — Sharing and files

| ID | Title | Module | Evidence | Deps | Blockers | Eff | Status / gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-103 | Public per-document links: token, expiry, revocation, access log, accept-quote | M4 | OQ-001 interim; portal sheet security rows | T-108a | — | M | **DONE** (schema v6 `public_links` + `public_link_access`; SHA-256 token digest only, 1–365-day expiry, revocation; `GET /api/public/documents/:token`, `/pdf`, `POST /accept`; owner routes create/list/revoke/access-log; public page `/p/:token`; « Partager » dialog on invoice and quote records; 4 unit tests; live 201/200/410/409 verified) |
| T-101 | Attachments for expense receipts and payment proofs (configurable size, default 10 MB) | M6 | BK-010; OQ-009 | T-100 | — (PQ-3 only affects showing a *hosting* ceiling; the configured cap is shown) | M | **DONE** — schema v8 `attachments` + `attachment_chunks`. The bytes are kept **in the workspace database, split into 256 KiB chunks**, so receipts work without an object bucket; the ceiling is a setting (`attachment_max_mb`, 1–25, default 10) clamped rather than refused when a stored value is absurd. `GET /api/attachments/limits`, `GET /api/attachments?entity=&entity_id=`, `POST /api/attachments` (base64), `GET /api/attachments/:id/download`, `DELETE /api/attachments/:id`. **The permission is the record's**: `expenses.read/write` for a receipt, `payments.read/write` for a proof, asserted through one helper that the route-guard invariant pins, so a read-only account can open a receipt and cannot remove one. The declared size is never trusted — the decoded bytes decide — and only PDF / JPEG / PNG / WebP are accepted, with the filename reduced to its last path segment. Downloads carry `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `nosniff` and `private, no-store`; deleting soft-deletes the row and drops the chunks, journalled as `activity.attachment_added|deleted`. UI: a « Justificatifs » action on every expense and payment row opens the same panel (list, download, add, remove), with the upload button gated by the write permission. 22 unit tests (ceiling clamp, filename traversal/control characters, empty/oversize/unsupported, base64 round-trip and refusal, chunk split/join at the boundaries, SHA-256 vector, header quoting). Live on the local D1 [EXECUTED]: limits 10 MB; 22-byte PDF uploaded 201; list shows « Ana Rey »; download 200 `application/pdf` with **identical SHA-256**; `text/html` 422 `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`; broken base64 422; unknown expense 404; ceiling lowered to 1 MB → 1.5 MB refused 422 with `max_bytes`; viewer lists 200 but delete 403; payment proof 201; delete 204 then list empty and download 404; anonymous 401; journal 2 added + 1 deleted. **Not claimed:** the MIME type is the browser's claim, not sniffed from the bytes (mitigated by never rendering inline); no antivirus scan; no browser walk of the panel; the 1.5 MB payload is the largest file this walk moved, so multi-chunk reassembly is proven by unit test rather than by a live 10 MB upload.

## Phase 4 — Automation

| ID | Title | Module | Evidence | Deps | Blockers | Eff | Status / gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-104a | Daily-run endpoint: secret token, rate limit, Tahiti-day idempotency | M5 | OQ-003 | T-100 | PQ-1 (the trigger stays external — that is the contract) | M | **DONE** — `POST /api/runs/daily`, authenticated by `DAILY_RUN_TOKEN` (platform secret) through `x-run-token` or `Authorization: Bearer`, compared in **constant time**. The route accepts **no session on purpose**, so a stolen browser cookie can never trigger generation. Missing secret → 503 `DAILY_RUN_TOKEN_MISSING`; missing or wrong token → 401 `INVALID_RUN_TOKEN`; **10 attempts per hour per IP** then 429 `RUN_RATE_LIMITED` with `retry_after` (sliding window, old attempts pruned). Idempotency is the **primary key** of `daily_runs`: the Tahiti day is claimed by a conditional `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a second call — or two concurrent schedulers — returns 200 `already_ran: true` with the first run's stored summary and writes nothing; a `failed` or `skipped` day stays retryable and only one caller wins the retry. Every real pass writes `activity.daily_run_completed` with counts and the caller's IP. Live [EXECUTED]: no token 401, wrong token 401, `Bearer` accepted 200, the 11th call in the window 429, restart without the secret 503. **Not claimed:** no real external scheduler was configured (PQ-1), and the 429 was measured from one address only. |
| T-104b | Run pipeline: recurring invoices + reminders + stored result | M5 | BK-003 | T-104a | Reminders are T-105 | M | **DONE for the recurring half** — the generation logic moved out of the manual route into `server/services/recurring.ts`, so the button and the pipeline cannot produce different invoices. The pass selects **active** templates only (a model is created as `draft`, so it never auto-generates before someone activates it — found by the walk, not by reading), joins the client for its payment terms, generates the **missed cycles** one by one so the numbering stays continuous, and stops at **12 cycles per template** and **50 templates per pass** (`truncated` says so instead of silently dropping work). Each template is handled separately: a failure is recorded as `{id, code}` without stopping the rest, and the run is stored as `success` / `partial` / `failed`; a **closed period** makes the pass `skipped` (`PERIOD_LOCKED`) rather than writing into locked books. The stored summary is what `already_ran` returns the rest of the day. Live [EXECUTED]: three active templates (one two months late, one due today, one due in November) → first pass generated **FAC-2026-0008 à 0011** (3 catch-up + 1 due today), invoice count 7 → 11, all `draft` (no auto-send) and linked to their template; second call the same day `already_ran` with count still 11. **Known behaviour, not fixed here:** the engine advances from the last date, so a template starting on the 31st drifts to the 28th (asserted by test); reminders ride this pipeline in T-105. |
| T-104c | Dashboard « dernier passage » card + manual run button | M5 | OQ-003 spec §5-6 | T-104b | — | S | **DONE** — the dashboard payload gains `last_run` (day, status, start/finish, stored summary) read from `daily_runs`, and the dashboard shows a « Passage quotidien » card: last result, its date, and the counts in French and English. A « Lancer maintenant » button calls `POST /api/runs/daily/manual` (`recurring.write`, session + CSRF), which **shares the day claim** with the machine endpoint — pressing it twice, or pressing it while the scheduler runs, still yields at most one pass; the card itself needs only `reports.read`, the dashboard's permission. Live [EXECUTED]: `/api/dashboard` returned `last_run` = 2026-10-29 / success / 0 reminder / 0 invoice for that pass; the manual call answered `already_ran: true` with the stored summary instead of regenerating; the same call **without the CSRF header** was refused 403. **Not claimed:** no browser walk of the card, and the button was only pressed on a day already run — the executing path of the manual route is the shared pipeline, proven by the scheduled walk, not by a second live call. |
| T-105 | Automatic reminders through the pipeline | M5 | BK-002 | T-104b | PQ-2 only for *sending* the message | S | **DONE (recorded)** — schema v10 `invoice_reminders` with a **unique pair (invoice, level)**, which is the memory the manual action never had: until now a reminder existed only as a journal line, so a daily pass would have nagged the same client every morning. Levels are 1 (the day after the due date), 2 and 3, one per interval; the interval is a setting (`reminder_interval_days`, 7 by default). A pass computes the level lateness warrants, records **every level still missing** (so a client who fell behind while the scheduler was off gets the sequence once, in order, not a single muddled entry), and journals `activity.reminder_automatic` per level. The manual « Relancer » action now records its level too, so the two paths cannot duplicate each other. Reminders ride the daily pass **after** invoice generation, so an invoice created this morning is never reminded the same breath. 10 unit tests (lateness thresholds and boundaries, cap at 3, a custom interval, a nonsense interval, missing-level computation, recorded levels not repeated). Live [EXECUTED]: two invoices set 10 days late → one pass recorded **3 levels** (1, 2, 3) with 3 journal entries; a following pass on the same data recorded **0** and the table still holds 3 rows; a manual reminder on a draft invoice was correctly refused 409 `INVOICE_NOT_OPEN`. **Not claimed:** **no message is sent** — PQ-2 still gates delivery, so a reminder is a recorded, auditable intention, not an e-mail; no UI shows the reminder history yet; the manual path was proven by its refusal and by unit tests, not by a live success on an overdue invoice. |
| T-106 | Outbound e-mail provider (key in platform Secrets) | M11 | BK-021; OQ-002 | T-105 | — (a *real* delivery still needs a provider credential and PQ-2) | M | **DONE (code)** — schema v7 `email_settings` (single workspace row): provider `manual` (default, nothing leaves), `resend`, `brevo` or an explicit SMTP relay, plus per-document-kind subject/body templates. Credentials are stored **AES-GCM encrypted** under `MAIL_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (platform secret, ≥ 32 chars) and never returned — the API exposes only `has_api_key` / `has_smtp_password`; platform secrets `RESEND_API_KEY` / `BREVO_API_KEY` / `SMTP_PASSWORD` take precedence over the stored ciphertext. SMTP is restricted on purpose: hostname validated (no IPv4, no `localhost` / `.local` / `.internal`, no embedded port) and only ports 465/587, which keeps the relay from being pointed at the platform itself. `GET/PUT /api/settings/email` and `POST /api/settings/email/test` require `settings.write` (manager-only, so the panel is not even readable by a read-only role); `POST /api/email/:kind/:id` requires the **document's** write permission, builds the PDF in the chosen layout, expands the template, journals `activity.<kind>_emailed`, and only flips a draft to `sent` **after** a successful dispatch. **Two defects found while resuming, both fixed:** the production build had been broken since the module landed (esbuild could not resolve `cloudflare:sockets` imported by `worker-mailer`; `build:worker` now marks `cloudflare:*` external), and `MailSecrets` did not declare the keys the dispatcher reads, which had forced two `as` casts. 28 unit tests (payload field by field for Resend and Brevo, escaping, credential round-trip/rotation/tampering, SMTP host and port rules, no network call when unconfigured) and a `FILE_LEVEL_GUARDS` entry so the per-document permission check cannot be dropped. Live on a fresh local D1 [EXECUTED]: anonymous 401; owner GET 200 `manual`; resend without credentials 422 `credentials: required`; with a key but no encryption secret 503 `MAIL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_MISSING`; SET without token 403 `CSRF_TOKEN`; viewer GET/PUT settings and POST send all 403; unknown kind and unknown document 404; manual send 409 `EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED` with the invoice **still `draft`**; with the secret set, save 200, GET reports `has_api_key: true` with no ciphertext, database holds `v1.` ciphertext (80 chars) for provider `resend`; a send with a deliberately invalid key answers 502 `EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED` and leaves the invoice `draft`; three `activity.email_settings_changed` entries journalled. **Not claimed:** no message has ever been delivered from this host — there is no provider credential, and a 502 does not distinguish a provider rejection from a blocked outbound call (egress was checked separately: Resend answers 401 without a key). **Not verified:** no browser walk of the Paramètres → E-mail panel; SMTP has never opened a socket.

## Why this order

1. **Parameters before anything that prints them** — T-100 closes the accountant blocker, so tax wording, retention and the franchise ceiling are settings, not assumptions. T-107 and T-010 ride on it.
2. **Document output before sharing** — a public link that cannot render a quote or a credit note would ship broken; T-108a then T-108 then T-103 is the only safe sequence.
3. **Storage before automation** — attachments (T-101) are independent, so they run beside the PDFs instead of blocking the scheduler.
4. **Automation is a chain** — endpoint, pipeline, dashboard, reminders, e-mail: each depends on the previous, and e-mail stays last because it alone needs a platform answer.
5. **Permissions before the admin screens** — role CRUD (T-202) decides what a « Voir » screen may show, so it precedes T-201 and the gating policy.
6. **Operations last** — bank matching, kanban, saved filters and local reports depend on documents, permissions and the fiscal defaults being settled.
